svg.title: Connect the adaptor to the oriented message
svg.desc: The mRNA codon5′-GAA-3′ aligns antiparallel with tRNA anticodon3′-CUU-5′, equivalently written5′-UUC-3′. This tRNA is charged with glutamate under the standard code. Codon and anticodon belong to different RNA molecules. Ribosomes contain ribosomal proteins and rRNA with structural and catalytic roles. A process sequence connects start/frame establishment, charged tRNA pairing and peptide-bond formation, movement along mRNA, stop-codon recognition by a release factor and chain release. There is no ordinary amino-acid-loaded stop tRNA or stop amino acid. Later folding, processing and stability are needed to infer functional protein accumulation.

g.text: Connect the adaptor to the oriented message
Antiparallel pairing supports translation but does not supply every step by itself.
A charged tRNA brings the appropriate amino acid: here, glutamate (Glu).
mRNA supplies the codon; tRNA supplies the anticodon and carried amino acid.
rRNA contributes structure and catalysis in the ribosome, together with ribosomal proteins.
Initiation establishes a suitable start/frame → elongation pairs tRNAs and forms peptide bonds
→ ribosome advances along mRNA → a stop codon recruits a release factor → chain is released.
No amino-acid-carrying “stop tRNA” adds an amino acid called stop.
Folding, processing, partners and stability still affect whether functional protein accumulates.
